items.followUp: Name the three states of equilibrium and give one example of stable equilibrium.

rubric.why: All three states of equilibrium are required.
rubric.description: Names stable, unstable and neutral equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for all three; 1 mark for any two.

modelAnswer: The three states of equilibrium are stable, unstable and neutral equilibrium.

items.followUp: Define mechanical energy and sound energy.

rubric.why: Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference.
rubric.description: Defines heat in terms of energy transfer due to temperature difference.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this defining idea.

rubric.why: Electrical energy is associated with electric charges or their flow.
rubric.description: Defines electrical energy as energy associated with electric charges or their flow.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

modelAnswer: Heat is energy transferred from a hotter body to a colder body due to a temperature difference.
Electrical energy is the energy associated with electric charges, particularly when they flow through a circuit.

items.followUp: Name and briefly describe the two processes by which nuclear energy is released.

rubric.why: Nuclear fission is one method of releasing nuclear energy.
rubric.description: Names nuclear fission.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying fission.

rubric.why: Nuclear fusion is the other method of releasing nuclear energy.
rubric.description: Names nuclear fusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying fusion.

modelAnswer: Nuclear energy is released by nuclear fission and nuclear fusion.

items.followUp: What is solar energy? State two of its uses.

rubric.why: Wind energy is the energy of moving air.
rubric.description: Defines wind energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying moving air or its kinetic energy.

rubric.why: The question asks for uses as well as the definition.
rubric.description: Gives a valid use of wind energy, such as generating electricity or pumping water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one or more valid uses.

modelAnswer: Wind energy is the kinetic energy of moving air.
It is used to generate electricity and to pump water using windmills.

items.followUp: What are the lower and upper fixed points of the Celsius scale?

rubric.why: The lower fixed point is the ice point at 0°C.
rubric.description: Identifies the lower fixed point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for melting ice/ice point at 0°C.

rubric.why: The upper fixed point is the steam point at 100°C.
rubric.description: Identifies the upper fixed point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for boiling water/steam point at 100°C.

modelAnswer: The lower fixed point is the temperature of pure melting ice at standard atmospheric pressure, 0°C.
The upper fixed point is the temperature of steam above boiling water at standard atmospheric pressure, 100°C.

items.followUp: State Newton’s third law of motion and explain it using the recoil of a gun.

rubric.why: The law describes action and reaction forces.
rubric.description: States that every action has a reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the action–reaction relationship.

rubric.why: The forces have equal magnitude.
rubric.description: States that action and reaction are equal in magnitude.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for equality of magnitude.

rubric.why: The forces act in opposite directions.
rubric.description: States that action and reaction are opposite in direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for opposite directions.

rubric.why: A relevant example demonstrates the law.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example, such as walking, swimming or gun recoil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid example.

modelAnswer: Newton’s third law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
The action and reaction forces act simultaneously on two different bodies.
When we walk, our foot pushes the ground backwards and the ground pushes us forwards.
These two forces are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

items.followUp: Describe translatory, rotatory and vibratory motion, giving an example of each.

rubric.why: Translatory motion is one of the main types of motion.
rubric.description: Names and describes translatory motion: all parts of a body move the same distance in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the name and a correct description.

rubric.why: Rotatory motion is one of the main types of motion.
rubric.description: Names and describes rotatory motion: a body turns about an axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the name and a correct description.

rubric.why: Vibratory motion is one of the main types of motion.
rubric.description: Names and describes vibratory motion: repeated to-and-fro motion about a mean position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the name and a correct description.

rubric.why: An example supports the types described.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of one or more types of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example.

modelAnswer: In translatory motion, all parts of a body move the same distance in the same direction; a train moving along a straight track is an example.
In rotatory motion, a body spins about an axis; a rotating fan is an example.
In vibratory motion, a body moves repeatedly to and fro about a mean position; a swinging pendulum is an example.
Translatory motion may be linear, circular or random, depending on the path followed.

items.followUp: A square plate has a side of 10 mm. Find the pressure exerted on it by a force of 20 N.

rubric.why: The side length must be converted to SI units.
rubric.description: Converts the given side to 0.020 m.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct SI conversion.

rubric.why: Pressure requires the area of the square face.
rubric.description: Calculates the area as 4.0 × 10⁻⁴ m².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct area with unit.

rubric.why: The correct pressure relation is required.
rubric.description: Writes the pressure formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for P = F/A.

rubric.why: Correct substitution uses the force and calculated area.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values into the formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution.

rubric.why: The final pressure must be calculated and expressed in pascals.
rubric.description: Gives the correct pressure, 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct numerical answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: side = 20 mm = 0.020 m; force, F = 40 N.
Area of the square, A = side² = (0.020 m)² = 4.0 × 10⁻⁴ m².
Pressure, P = F/A.
Therefore, the pressure on the pin head is 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa.
